rationale: The case history uses Orange as part of Agent Orange, a historical exposure. The author's medication and supplement case provides no raw-orange or fall-frequency comparison. The journal retracted the report.
The single medication and supplement case discussed symptom and treatment histories without a dried-date comparison or a separately measured pain outcome. The journal retracted the report.

The published instrument includes painful sensations and asks about levodopa ON and OFF state. It was developed through patient-caregiver groups and expert review. It provides no dried-date comparison.

The instrument asks about loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities and its timing relative to levodopa. This questionnaire item is narrower than a separately contrasted clinical apathy score. No dried-date exposure.
The nonrandom pilot measured whole UPDRS motor and functional subscores, with no significant overall clinical interaction. It did not isolate rigidity or compare ground sage.
The six-month exercise group improved stride length relative to its baseline and the group by time interaction was p=.005. Allocation was nonrandom and ground sage was not tested.

Postmortem pharyngeal histology included eight PD donors and four controls. Clinical swallowing history and fiber atrophy are related to swallowing but there is no drooling severity measure or raw-fig comparison.
The clinical tables include total motor UPDRS III and dysphagia. Histology evaluates pharyngeal fibers. It gives no rest-tremor item comparison and no raw-fig exposure.

The original 48-hour protocol tests digit span and polysomnography in Parkinson disease and DLB. Customary meals were provided. It gives no fig intervention or visual hallucination frequency comparison.
The original outcomes distinguish forward and backward digit span and quantified sleep. There is no raw-fig exposure assignment or rest-tremor outcome contrast.
The Parkinson case-control gait and short-latency afferent inhibition study related gait speed to inhibition and attention. It does not quantify visual hallucination frequency or compare dried fig.
Resting tremor above the MDS-UPDRS screening threshold was an exclusion for inhibition testing. The study measures gait and inhibition rather than tremor change, with no raw-fig exposure.
Original Table 3 reports pain in 76.8% of PD without probable RBD and 85.0% with probable RBD. The table is symptom presence by sleep phenotype, with no dried-date comparison.
Original Table 3 reports apathy in 13.5% of PD without probable RBD and 22.8% with probable RBD. The baseline association does not assign dried-date intake or establish an exposure effect.
The original analysis covers PDQ-39 bodily discomfort in a quality-of-life subdomain. The trait anxiety association is not an isolated prescribed food or a separately tabulated pain-severity effect.

In 107 people with PD the Apathy Scale is a distinct measure. Apathy correlated with PDQ-39 summary scores (r=.241), while trait anxiety accounted for most independent variation. No dried-date exposure.
Pain is listed in the limitations among reasons for complementary medicine use that the authors did not ask about. The survey delivers no dried-date or pain severity comparison.
Apathy is discussed as a possible cannabis adverse effect requiring future examination. The survey offers no apathy measure or dried-date exposure.

Nocturnal sialorrhea was one possible enrollment complaint. The outcome assessments measured swallowing structures or penetration and aspiration after test boluses rather than drooling severity after raw fig.
The ultrasound protocol used water and the fluoroscopy used texture-defined contrast boluses. It measured swallowing anatomy and safety, without a rest-tremor or raw-fig outcome comparison.
Open-label PD AADC gene-therapy follow-up reports two subjects with insomnia as adverse events, Table 1; no sage intervention or sage-exposed comparison.
AADC gene-therapy follow-up lists falling in ten subjects and fractures in discussion, without a sage exposure or randomized food comparison.
PD telephone-use cohort of 175 compares BDI by calling frequency, 11.4 versus 9.3, p=.08, not by lemon balm intake.
Table 1 records off-dystonia in 20 frequent versus 17 infrequent callers; no lemon balm intervention or exposure comparison.
Randomized 130-person exercise versus usual-care economic evaluation uses EQ-5D pain/discomfort within aggregate utility; neither a dried-date intervention nor ingredient-specific pain contrast.
PD exercise cost study includes anxiety/depression in the aggregate EQ-5D utility, not anxiety following poached salmon or any assigned food.
Cross-sectional PD cognitive and ADL study uses PDQ-39 body pain domain but has no dried-date exposure or food comparison.
Neuropsychiatric Inventory assesses apathy among other domains in PD cognitive-impairment groups; this is not an assigned or observed dried-date intervention.
Ten-patient intraoperative STN stimulation fMRI paper discusses chronic pain as background and measures BOLD signals, not pain response to dried dates.
The paper measures DBS-associated BOLD activation; apathy worsening is cited from other reports and no dietary date exposure is reported.
NCT02231073 is a PD exercise versus education protocol; pain is an educational topic, not a reported dried-date pain comparison.
Protocol states rest tremor in PD diagnostic criteria and excludes severe tremor for imaging; no fig intervention or fig-tremor result.
Twenty-six PD patients and 26 controls underwent neuropathy assessments including King PD pain and McGill scales; no dried-date exposure or dietary pain comparison.
Small-fiber and motor assessments compare PD patients with controls, with UPDRS-III total, not raw-fig-specific rest-tremor severity.
Longitudinal PD cost study reports pain VAS and cost association, not a dried-date comparison; mean pain 19.2 at year 1 and 22.9 at year 4.
Longitudinal PD cost paper discusses resting tremor as a symptom in background, without an individual fig exposure or fig-specific tremor analysis.
Subcutaneous apomorphine in 57 levodopa-treated patients; one reported improvement in off-period hallucinations without modality specified, not dried-fig consumption.
The injection series reports relief of off-period limb and pelvic pain in three patients; there is no dried-date exposure or food comparison.
C9orf72 parkinsonism case series reports visual hallucinations during dopamine agonist treatment; it does not examine dried fig consumption or hallucination frequency as a food effect.
Genetic parkinsonism series describes rest tremor at onset in several patients and tabulates signs; no raw fig exposure or comparison.
DBS versus best medical therapy trial reports a pain-related SF-36 proxy, with less reported pain under DBS; no dried-date intervention or analysis.
Randomized DBS psychiatric study discusses apathy increase in a separate previously published medication-reduction study; no dried-date assessment.
Aneurysm-coiling case reports stumbling without falls and later levodopa-responsive parkinsonism; no raw orange exposure or fall-frequency intervention.
Case describes 5-Hz rest and postural tremor after cyst expansion, followed by levodopa response; raw fig is not studied.
Three Perry syndrome families include an intermittent upper-limb rest tremor case; Turkey is a country in prior-family background, not a baked turkey intervention.
Clinical Perry syndrome family reports include apathy; no dried-date intake, assigned diet or apathy food comparison.
Japanese family LRRK2 mutation and parkinsonism report presents clinical/genetic findings; no dried dates or pain comparison by food intake.
LRRK2 familial Parkinson report tabulates presence and absence of resting tremor by case, not tremor severity after raw fig consumption.
Ghanaian and Italian PD cohorts compare clinical phenotype and levodopa-related motor complications; tremor-dominant phenotype is not a raw-fig intervention.
Table 2 reports combined depression/apathy at baseline in Ghanaian and Italian cohorts; no dried-date dietary comparison.
Analysis of 423 untreated early PD PPMI participants predicts initiation of symptomatic medication from clinical scores; no ground sage exposure or rigidity comparison.
The MDS-UPDRS tremor subscore combines 11 items and predicts medication initiation; this is not a measured raw-fig rest-tremor effect.
